title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Microsoft Copilot usage report for GCC High and DoD
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, reporting metrics, privacy setting and automation are supported. Microsoft Learn gives two different routes to the report; the briefing's route matches the report's own page, but should acknowledge the alternative in the reporting overview.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a new Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): Microsoft 365 admin center – New Microsoft 365 Copilot usage report for GCC High & DoD

claims.where: What's changing; licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Enabled Users counts unique users with Microsoft Copilot licences over the selected timeframe.
claims.quote: Enabled Users shows the total number of unique users in your organization with Microsoft Copilot licenses over the selected timeframe.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Active Users counts enabled users who tried a user-initiated Copilot feature in one or more Microsoft 365 apps over the selected timeframe.
claims.quote: Active Users shows the total number of enabled users in your organization who tried a user-initiated Microsoft Copilot feature, in one or more apps in Microsoft 365 over the selected timeframe.

claims.claim: The report has an adoption-by-app chart.
claims.quote: In the Adoption section, Adoption by app shows enabled users and active users of Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps.

claims.claim: The report includes prompts submitted.
claims.quote: Total prompts submitted shows the total number of prompts users sent to Microsoft Copilot Chat during the selected time frame.

claims.claim: The report includes Copilot Chat adoption.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat adoption shows enabled users and total usage of Copilot Chat and split usage between Copilot Chat (work) and Copilot Chat (web).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The report includes a user-level last-activity table.
claims.quote: You can view a table list to show each Microsoft Copilot enabled user's last activity date among Microsoft Copilot apps.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The report timeframes are 7, 28, 90 and 180 days.
claims.quote: You can view the Microsoft Copilot report over the last 7, 28, 90, or 180 days.

claims.claim: Activity for a day typically becomes available within 48 hours of the end of that day in UTC.
claims.quote: For Copilot activity on a given day, the report typically becomes available within 48 hours of the end of that day (in UTC).

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Usage reports hide identifying user information such as usernames, display names, groups and sites by default.
claims.quote: By default, user-specific information like usernames, display names, groups, and sites is hidden in usage reports.

claims.claim: Global administrators can change the org setting to show identifying information.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The report and Copilot reporting options pages give roles rather than an administrator viewer licence.
claims.quote: To use the reporting features described in this article, you need to sign into different portals with the appropriate permissions. ... Microsoft 365 admin center ... AI Administrator: Accesses the Copilot reports.

claims.claim: No meter or charge for the report itself is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot usage report administrator viewing license requirements pricing meter. Opened report, usage reports overview, Copilot reporting options and Meters for Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go services; no report-viewing meter or charge is given.

claims.quote: In Recommendations, the recommended action card highlights Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, where you can deliver insights to your IT leaders to explore Copilot readiness, adoption, and impact in Viva Insights.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Showing identifiable user information is logged in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.
claims.quote: Showing identifiable user information is a logged event in the Microsoft Purview portal audit log.

claims.claim: Aggregated audit-log metrics might not agree with official Copilot usage reports.
claims.quote: Any aggregated metrics that you build on top of this data, such as "prompt count" or "active user count," might not be consistent with the corresponding data points in the official Copilot usage reports provided by Microsoft.

claims.claim: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote and Outlook Copilot client event uploads can be delayed.
claims.quote: For various reasons, uploading client events data for Copilot features in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, and Outlook can be delayed.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes activity reporting and does not state organizational messaging availability in GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: This report will include total enabled and active users, Copilot usage with a breakout per Microsoft 365 app, and user-level activity insights (anonymized by default). #copilotcontrolsystem

claims.claim: The report is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Copilot > Usage tab.
claims.quote: On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Copilot. ... select the Usage tab. Reporting options instead says: Select Microsoft Copilot > Readiness or Usage.
claims.fix: Keep the existing route and append: 'The Copilot reporting options overview gives an alternative route: Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot > Usage (https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/manage/copilot-admin-reports#microsoft-365-admin-center-reports).'

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The name-concealment setting is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: select Settings ... Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings updates the name-concealment control through displayConcealedNames.
claims.quote: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings ... displayConcealedNames ... If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The concealment setting is tenant-wide and applies across Microsoft 365 usage reports, including Copilot, rather than being Copilot-specific.
claims.quote: Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports. ... If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The setting also applies to Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI.
claims.quote: This setting also applies to the Microsoft 365 usage reports in Microsoft Graph and Power BI and to the usage reports in Microsoft Teams Admin center.

claims.claim: The cited Graph API is documented in beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.
